LHX.sentence: L3Harris is down roughly a quarter from its high, which is unusually steep for a steady defense contractor — but military spending keeps rolling along, so this looks more like the stock falling out of favor than anything wrong with the business.

ASML.sentence: ASML ticked up a bit and sits about 11% below its high — a quiet stretch for the only company on earth that makes the machines needed to print the most advanced chips.

LIN.sentence: Linde is having a quiet, uneventful stretch — they supply industrial gases under long contracts and nudge prices up a little each quarter, which is really the whole story with this one.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft has held up far better than the other big tech names lately, as its cloud and AI business keeps grinding along without drama.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher rose a bit and is trading near its high even though its profit margins are still depressed — meaning a lot of hope for a lab-spending recovery is already baked into the price.

CVX.sentence: Chevron slipped slightly; oil is well above normal right now because fighting involving Iran has disrupted Persian Gulf shipments, so its profits are swollen by the oil price rather than by anything the company itself did.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow has fallen more than 40% from its high, which is a lot for a company still growing fast — big companies and government agencies keep signing on for its workflow and AI tools, so this is fear getting ahead of the business.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore drifted lower, but between its mining and its huge commodity-trading arm it's paying out a hefty chunk of cash to shareholders, which gives the stock a solid floor.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta dipped a touch, and while the headline price per ton looks like it fell, that's just a mix of what sold — the real price they get for a ton of crushed stone is still creeping up, which is the part that matters.

KOF.sentence: Coca-Cola FEMSA is steady, though a weakening Mexican peso trims the value of its earnings when converted back to dollars — a currency headwind rather than a problem with the bottling business itself.

UBER.sentence: Uber barely moved, and the key number is that people keep booking about 20% more rides than a year ago — no sign yet that self-driving cars are pulling business away, with the next big update due in early November.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk is quiet and its shares are priced below what its own fleet of ships would cost to replace, a sign of how cheap it's gotten even with too many container ships sailing the world right now.

MA.sentence: Mastercard slipped a bit and is priced almost in line with Visa for once, but people keep tapping their cards more than ever, so there's no real problem in the business itself.

ISRG.sentence: The surgical robot maker rose a little and is down about a quarter from its high — a deep fear setup, even though hospitals are still expected to do far more operations with its machines and there's no proof it's losing ground to rivals.

NVDA.sentence: Nvidia rose on the day, but the real worry is that two of its biggest customers — Google's parent and Amazon — are now spending more on computing gear than their businesses bring in and borrowing the rest, so the question is whether those customers can keep paying, not anything about Nvidia itself.
